newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB shares see wild gains on gold speculation.
newsitem.headline: SNB shares see wild gains on gold speculation.

text.p: Speculation linked to the Swiss National Bank's (SNB) plan to revalue its gold reserves and proposed constitutional changes which would allow greater flexibility in its investment policy has led to a leap in the central bank's shares.
The share price was up more than 57 percent at 1,300 francs in afternoon Swiss Bourse trading versus Tuesday's close.
"It (the price rise) has to do with rather unrealistic expectations regarding the gold reserves," SNB spokesman Werner Abegg said.

The Swiss government, in response to charges that the Swiss coldly profited from World War Two, in March proposed creation of a humanitarian fund that would use Swiss official gold reserves to aid victims of human rights abuses, catastrophes and the Holocaust.

The foundation would be financed by a substantial proportion of profits achieved by revaluing gold the central bank now has on its books to about 60 percent of current market prices. It is currently valued at less than a third of market prices.
"There seem to be shareholders who expect they can directly benefit," Abegg said.
He also said the SNB's share price tended to move erratically in tandem with big moves in gold prices in the international markets.
The Swiss central bank has 100,000 shares outstanding. Some 63 percent of the total are held by Swiss cantons, cantonal banks and other public agencies.
There are only 451 shares, or 0.45 percent of the share capital in foreign hands and these shares do not carry voting rights.
